trash.title: Competitive Equilibrium with Tax
trash.content:
\paragraph{Pigouvian Tax II: Taxing consumption of good $y^1$}

The problem of agent 1 with tax $\textcolor{red}{\tau}$ becomes
\[
\max_{y^1,x^1} \; u^1(y^1) + x^1
\]
\[
\text{s.t.} \quad (p + \textcolor{red}{\tau})y^1 + x^1 
\le p\omega_y^1 + \omega_x^1 + T^1.
\]

This delivers the first order condition for agent 1:
\[
\frac{d u^1(y^1)}{d y^1} = p^* + \textcolor{red}{\tau},
\]

while agent 2 maximises $u^2(y^2) + x^2$ subject to
\[
p y^2 + x^2 \le p\omega_y^2 + \omega_x^2 + T^2
\]
and hence would satisfy:
\[
\frac{d u^2(y^2)}{d y^2} = p^*.
\]

\medskip

Recall that the planner's first order conditions are:
\[
\frac{d u^1(y^{1*})}{d y^1}
-
\frac{d \phi(y^{1*})}{d y^1}
=
\frac{d u^2(y^{2*})}{d y^2}
=
\mu_y^*.
\]

Equivalently,
\[
\frac{d u^1(y^{1*})}{d y^1}
=
\mu_y^* + \frac{d \phi(y^{1*})}{d y^1},
\qquad
\frac{d u^2(y^{2*})}{d y^2}
=
\mu_y^*.
\]

If we now set
\[
\textcolor{red}{\tau^* = \frac{d\phi(y^{1*})}{d y^1} > 0}
\quad \text{and} \quad
p^* = \mu_y^*,
\]
then the competitive first order conditions become

\[
\frac{d u^1(y^{1*})}{d y^1}
=
p^* + \textcolor{red}{\tau^*}
=
\mu_y^* + \frac{d \phi(y^{1*})}{d y^1},
\]

\[
\frac{d u^2(y^{2*})}{d y^2}
=
p^*
=
\mu_y^*.
\]

Hence the private optimality conditions coincide exactly with the planner’s optimality conditions. 
By strict concavity of $u^1$ and $u^2$, these choices are unique, so consumer 1 chooses $y^{1*}$ and agent 2 chooses $y^{2*}$.

Finally, setting
\[
T^1 + T^2 = \textcolor{red}{\tau^* y^{1*}}
\]
rebates tax revenues in a lump-sum way, ensuring feasibility and market clearing without affecting marginal conditions.

\[
\textcolor{red}{\text{We implement the social optimum as a CE with taxes.}}
\]

trash.title: Market for Externalities
trash.content:
\paragraph{Market for Externalities I: Supply.}

Suppose consumer 2 can prevent agent 1’s choice of $y^1$ and 
\textcolor{red}{can sell the right to undertake 1 unit of $y^1$ for a price of $r$.}

\[
\max_{y^2,z^s,x^2} \; u^2(y^2) - \phi(\textcolor{red}{z^s}) + x^2
\]

\[
\text{s.t.} \quad
p y^2 + x^2 \le p\omega_y^2 + \omega_x^2 + \textcolor{red}{r z^s},
\]

where $z^s$ is the amount of externality rights that agent 2 sells.  
The agent correctly forecasts that all rights will be used, hence:
\[
\textcolor{red}{y^1 = z^s}.
\]

FOC (recall $\lambda^* = 1$):
\[
\frac{d u^2(y^2(p))}{d y^2} = p
\qquad \text{and} \qquad
\frac{d \phi(z^s(r))}{d z} = r.
\]

Rightmost condition implicitly defines a 
\textcolor{red}{supply function $z^s(r)$}.  
By convexity of $\phi$, $z^s(r)$ increases in $r$.

\vspace{1cm}

\paragraph{Market for Externalities II: Demand.}

In deciding how many rights to purchase, consumer 1 maximises

\[
\max_{y^1,z^d,x^1} \; u^1(y^1) + x^1
\]

\[
\text{s.t.} \quad
p y^1 + \textcolor{red}{r z^d} + x^1 \le p\omega_y^1 + \omega_x^1;
\qquad (\lambda)
\]

\[
y^1 \le \textcolor{red}{z^d}. 
\qquad (\xi)
\]

To consume $y^1$, agent 1 needs to buy both the goods themselves 
(at usual price $p$) and the externality rights (at price $r>0$).

FOC:
\[
\lambda^* = 1; 
\qquad 
\xi^* = r; 
\qquad 
y^{1*} = z^d;
\qquad
\frac{d u^1(z^d(r+p))}{d z} = p + r.
\]

which implicitly defines a 
\textcolor{red}{demand function: $z^d(r+p)$}.  

The market-clearing condition says that
\[
z^* = z^s(r^*) = z^d(r^* + p^*).
\]

If we set $\hat y^1 = z^*$ we have:
\[
\frac{d u^1(\hat y^1)}{d y^1}
=
\frac{d u^2(\hat y^2)}{d y^2}
+
\frac{d \phi(\hat y^1)}{d y^1}.
\]

trash.title: Public Goods
Planner Problem
trash.content:
The Planner solves (recall, thanks to quasilinear preferences, we can use equal Pareto weights)

\[
\max_{x^1,x^2,y} \; u^1(y) + x^1 + u^2(y) + x^2 \quad \text{s.t.} \quad
x^1 + x^2 + c(y) \le \omega^1 + \omega^2
\qquad (\mu).
\]

to produce y units of the public good, you must use c(y) units of x.

The optimality conditions deliver $\mu^* = 1$ and:

\[
\frac{d u^1(y^*)}{dy}
+
\frac{d u^2(y^*)}{dy}
=
c'(y^*).
\tag{2}
\]

trash.title: Competitive Equilibrium
trash.content:
CE where agents can privately purchase the public good at a given price $p$. 
Public good is produced by a private firm owned by agents in equal shares:

\[
\max_{x^i,y^i} \; u^i(y^i + \hat y^{-i}) + x^i
\]

\[
\text{s.t.} \quad
x^i + p y^i \le \omega^i + \frac{1}{2}\hat\pi.
\qquad (\lambda^i)
\]

FOC:
\[
\frac{d u^i(\hat y)}{d y^i}
\le \hat p
\quad \text{with equality if } \hat y^i > 0,
\]

where
\[
\hat y = \hat y^1 + \hat y^2.
\]

NB: When choosing $y^i$ agent $i$ is guessing other agent choice $\hat y^{-i}$.  
The idea is that agents are guessing the ‘aggregate amount’ $\hat y$.

The firm solves the following profit maximisation problem:

\[
\pi = \max_{y} \; py - c(y).
\]

The FOC of the firm delivers the supply schedule of the public good; in a CE we have:
\[
c'(\hat y) = \hat p.
\]

\[
\hat \pi = \hat p \hat y - c(\hat y)
= c'(\hat y)\hat y - c(\hat y) > 0
\qquad \text{[Why?]}
\]

Bringing the two conditions together, we have 
$$\textcolor{blue}{\frac{du^1}{dy}\ge\frac{d u^2}{dy}}$$

\[
\frac{d u^1(\hat y)}{dy^1}
=
c'(\hat y)
\ge
\frac{d u^2(\hat y)}{dy^2}.
\]

\textcolor{red}{
If they have different utilities, the one with lower marginal utility at the equilibrium level free rides.
}

Incompatible with the Pareto optimal condition.

Given the concavity of $u^1$ and the convexity of $c$, 
\textcolor{red}{the public good is under provided in a CE: $\hat y < y^*$.}  

\textcolor{blue}{Agent 2 free rides on agent 1.}

trash.title: Solutions to the Public Good Problem
trash.content:
\paragraph{Solutions to the Public Good Problem.}

\begin{itemize}
    \item Using the Pigouvian taxation example from the bilateral externality case. 
    \textcolor{red}{Individual specific subsidy (positive externality)}
    \[
    \textcolor{red}{
    s^1 = \frac{d u^2(y^*)}{dy}
    \quad \text{and} \quad
    s^2 = \frac{d u^1(y^*)}{dy}.
    }
    \]

    \item Each consumer solves
    \[
    \max \quad u^i(y^i + y^{*-i}) + x^i
    \]
    \[
    \text{s.t.} \quad
    (p - s^i)y^i + x^i \le \omega^i + \frac{1}{2}\pi^*.
    \]

    \item FOC
    \[
    \frac{d u^i(y)}{dy^i} = p - s^i.
    \]

    Firm FOC and market-clearing:
    \[
    c'(y) = p = \frac{d u^1(y)}{dy} + \frac{d u^2(y)}{dy}.
    \]

    which is satisfied when $y = y^*$.
\end{itemize}

trash.title: Lindahl Equilibrium
trash.content:
The competitive equilibrium can be reached with personalized prices for a public good such that each individual’s marginal willingness to pay equals their personalized price, and the sum of prices equals marginal cost.

But you should know what is for each person its willingness to pay!...
